tagline: Up the Ocoee Gorge to the Copper Basin.
intro: US 64 picks up the Ocoee at Parksville, where the river comes out of the mountains into the Tennessee Valley, and winds east past Parksville Lake and up between the rocky bluffs of the gorge. On the cliffs along the south side, a wooden flume built for a dam of 1913 carries water five miles before dropping it into a powerhouse.

This was the first national forest scenic byway in the country. At its upper end the road reaches Ducktown, in the Copper Basin, which mined copper from 1847 until 1987. Cherokee who hid in these mountains to escape removal later helped build the Old Copper Road, now part of US 64.

moments.title: Parksville Lake
moments.text: The road passes just north of Ocoee Dam No. 1, finished in 1911 as one of Tennessee's first hydroelectric projects, which backs the river up into the lake.

moments.title: Chilhowee Scenic Spur
moments.text: Forest Road 77 climbs seven miles to the Chilhowee Recreation Area, with overlooks reaching across the Tennessee Valley to the Cumberland Mountains and into the mountains of Georgia.

moments.title: Ocoee Whitewater Center
moments.text: The canoe slalom course of the 1996 Olympics, the only Olympic slalom course ever laid in a river itself, sits on a stretch of the Upper Ocoee that is dry most of the year.
